topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's aims and sets out the key themes regarding cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how clonal progression is driven by the selection of advantageous genetic mutations and alterations in the epigenetic landscape.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell models of tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the contribution of tissue hierarchy and cell of origin to tumor initiation across blood and intestinal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how external environmental promoters and chronic inflammation cooperate with driver mutations to enable tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Microenvironmental dependency in established tumors and therapeutic avenues
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how established tumors depend on their supportive stromal microenvironment and how this dependency can be therapeutically targeted.

topics.label: Technologies for investigating tumor evolution and microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the multifactorial nature of cancer evolution and conclude the session.
